purpose: Screen the ACIS 21500 third SAB/SAT header integer against published ACIS 7.0 material, a newer open-source format description, and the current source-bound 21500 record census without promoting an unsupported version-wide meaning.
question: Does the ACIS 21500 third header integer count bodies, saved top-level entities, or identify the first owned-record boundary?

references.title: ACIS SAT File Format, SAT Format 7.0, Save File Header and Entity Records
references.finding: The third integer is described as a count of entities in the original entity list saved to the part file. Top-level entities are stated to occupy the first records.
references.versionScope: SAT Format 7.0 / ACIS 7.0; this is not direct ACIS 21.5 evidence.

references.title: cadmpeg ASM and ACIS kernel stream format specification
references.finding: For its explicitly scoped ACIS 217/218 widths, the entity-count word is the RecordTable index of the first owned record: asmheader is index 0, saved top-level entities occupy indices 1 through entity_count exclusive, and the first owned record is at entity_count.
references.versionScope: ACIS 217/218 only; not evidence for ACIS 215.

references.title: Working with .sat and .sab Files in Teigha (Open Design Alliance)
references.finding: Maps AutoCAD R24/2010 to SAT/SAB version 21500 and says AutoCAD versions 20800 and later use modified SAT/SAB formats that are not native to Spatial ACIS and require additional conversion before use by the Spatial ACIS library.
references.versionScope: Confirms the Autodesk-modified format family and release mapping; it does not define the third header integer.

sourceObservations.source: Hash-pinned AC1024 visualization aerial 3DSOLID 0x183; SAB SHA-256 00f7dd11b8993d066a25e33a05dd97fb14f8b35eb7a4d7614c596b6b41d6d79b
sourceObservations.interpretation: The value 2 equals the exclusive index of the first owned record in this observed row, but this one-source equality does not establish 21500 field semantics.

sourceObservations.source: Hash-pinned local AC1024 visualization conference-room 3DSOLID 0x1FB; SAB SHA-256 bd3232ad504732b311f70b4280f294f1dbd38d77794910fda2cce393ebc1267b
sourceObservations.interpretation: A second source-distinct one-body case also has value 2; it does not distinguish body-count from saved-entity/boundary interpretations. Producer metadata is not independently authenticated.

conclusion: The evidence makes a saved top-level-entity or first-owned-record-boundary interpretation more plausible than a literal body count for the observed records, because both contain asmheader plus one body and declare 2. The ODA source establishes that 21500 is in AutoCAD's modified-format family, which further weakens direct transfer of native Spatial ACIS 7.0 semantics; the 217/218 implementation is also cross-version evidence. No version-specific 21500 semantic rule is admitted.
implementationDecision: Do not rename the field as a body count, validate it against body records, derive a source boundary from it, or change SAT output behavior. Preserve the raw integer. Require a version-qualified 21500 producer/schema witness, preferably including a multi-root case, before semantic use.
claimEffect: Narrows the hypothesis space and documents why the two existing one-body samples are nondiscriminating. Does not close the 21500 header gate or promote parser, output, B-rep, native, platform, or support claims.
limitations: The available ACIS 7.0 reference predates ACIS 21.5.
ODA identifies 21500 as an Autodesk-modified SAT/SAB format, but its public article does not define the third header field.
The cadmpeg specification is scoped to 217/218, not 215.
Both local AC1024 sources have one rooted body and raw third integer 2.
No authenticated ACIS 21.5 producer, SDK header definition, or independent multi-root source was found in this screen.
The local conference-room DWG remains outside the repository and no sample fixture was added.
